notes: Most common carbapenemase in K. pneumoniae in many regions; CARD lists K. pneumoniae as the source organism of KPC-2.
NDM-1 was first described in K. pneumoniae (CARD ARO:3000589).
VIM variants are reported in K. pneumoniae (CARD prevalence data).
OXA-48 and OXA-181/OXA-232 are found in K. pneumoniae (CARD).
CTX-M-15 is the dominant ESBL in K. pneumoniae.
Plasmid AmpC in K. pneumoniae is often DHA-type rather than CMY; CMY is used here as the representative plasmid AmpC family.
MCR genes occur in K. pneumoniae (CARD lists MCR-7.1 from a K. pneumoniae isolate) but colistin resistance in K. pneumoniae is mostly chromosomal (mgrB/pmrAB) and is not modelled.
armA and rmt genes are distributed in Enterobacterales and often travel with NDM.
KPC is reported in E. coli but less often than in K. pneumoniae.
NDM-5 is frequent in E. coli.
VIM is reported in E. coli but is uncommon; reviewer to confirm it belongs in scope.
OXA-244 and OXA-181 occur in E. coli.
CTX-M-15 and CTX-M-14/27 are the main ESBLs in E. coli.
CMY-2 is the most common plasmid AmpC in E. coli (CARD lists several CMY alleles from E. coli).
mcr-1 is best described in E. coli.
armA and rmtB occur in E. coli.
Main acquired carbapenemase of carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB).
NDM-1 is reported in A. baumannii but is much less common than OXA-23-like enzymes.
armA is widespread in A. baumannii.
VIM-2 is the most common carbapenemase in P. aeruginosa; CARD describes VIM-1 as found in Pseudomonas spp.
NDM is reported in some P. aeruginosa lineages; reviewer to confirm relevance.
CARD lists P. aeruginosa among KPC-2 hosts; KPC-producing P. aeruginosa is regional (e.g. parts of South America).

mechanism_name: PDC beta-lactamase (chromosomal AmpC overproduction in P. aeruginosa)
notes: PDC is chromosomal in all P. aeruginosa; the mechanism modelled is its derepression or overproduction.
Loss of the OprD porin is the main route to imipenem resistance in P. aeruginosa without a carbapenemase.
rmt genes (for example rmtD) are reported in P. aeruginosa; not confirmed against CARD prevalence data.
mecA encodes PBP2a and defines MRSA; the CARD family also contains mecC.
